newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent soars as U.S./Iraq conflict escalates.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent soars as U.S./Iraq conflict escalates.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures rallied by 70 cents per barrel on Wednesday following Iraqi missile attacks on U.S. fighter planes in Iraq and American moves to bolster its military arsenal in the Gulf, brokers said. October Brent closed 70 cents up at $23.59 per barrel, having touched a post-Gulf War high of $23.82 during the day. The contract has gained $1.50 in the past week.

"It's up on the missiles in Iraq and the talk of another strike. It may be getting over-extended, but there is no negative news in the market and that allows locals to exploit it to the upside," a broker said.

The tension in the Gulf was still escalating at the close, as U.S. defense secretary William Perry hinted that U.S. reprisals were imminent, and that any U.S. response to Iraq's missile attack would be "disproportionate" to the attack.
In addition to moving B-52 bombers to a British Indian Ocean air base, Perry said the U.S. was moving eight F-117A "stealth" fighters to Kuwait.

"The Iraqi news was just a catalyst for an already strong market," said a broker, citing the latest U.S. API inventory data which showed falling crude and gasoline stocks, and a continuing year-on-year shortfall in distillates.
He said the risk of a 24-hour Brazilian oilworkers strike on September 26 added more fuel to the rally.

However, another broker sounded a word of warning: "The market is very vulnerable to the downside," he said. "Once the ball starts rolling, there is a vast potential drop in store, but there is no sign of that yet."
IPE September gas oil, which is due to expire on Thursday, ended $3.75 higher at $221.50 per tonne.
The Sept/Oct spread shed $1.50 to $5.00 backwardation as traders liquidated their length in the spread which last week touched a high of $9.25.
The October Brent/gas oil crack spread closed at $5.60 per barrel on Wednesday, 20 cents off its latest high, but still far above its recent low of $4.15 on August 19.
